text:
Detroit comes to Colorado on the wrong side of a one-goal game: the Red Wings lost 2-1 to Vegas on a goal with 1:42 left, their third loss in five. They're without captain Dylan Larkin (suspension, ESPN's estimated return Nov 14), and Alex DeBrincat has taken his spot beside Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson while Emmitt Finnie has moved onto the first power-play unit. Colorado lost 3-2 in overtime to Nashville, where Vitali Pinchuk scored his first NHL goal, and is 3-1-1 over its last five without Josh Manson.

The teams grade out almost evenly at five on five, each at 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). Colorado creates a little more, 3.40 expected goals per 60 against Detroit's 3.24, and gives up fewer, and its penalty kill is the stingier one. Our model has the Avalanche scoring 3.28 tonight to Detroit's 2.87. Both projected goalies have struggled this year: John Gibson (DET) is at -6.3 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots should allow), Mackenzie Blackwood (COL) at -0.5, though both were positive last season.

Watch Nathan MacKinnon, 40% to score and 85% for a point, and Arvidsson, who plays his 700th game. Finnie plays his 100th, and Prashanth Iyer of Expected By Whom posted that the Wings have "finally found" their 1C in him. Our under-the-radar pick is COL's T.J. Hughes, 41% for a point against a 34% season pace, because his line creates chances.
